To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method for determining the energetics and kinetics of allosteric proteins, which we applied to a K+ channel RCK domain to obtain a model that quantitively predicts its Ca2+ dependence.
the Ca2+-induced conformational changes that regulate the gating of MthK are driven by a large enthalpy and a large entropy.

(i) we have determined the energetics underlying conformational changes that occur in a single RCK domain from the MthK potassium channel; (ii) we have deduced an analytic model that predicts the open probability behavior of this channel from the energetics; and (iii) we have demonstrated that this model accurately predicts the channel’s Ca2+ dependence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energetics underlying the Ca2+-induced conformational changes that regulate MthK.
the energetics and mechanisms of conformational changes that occur in the RCK domains of the Mthk K+ channel.
the energetics and dynamics of allosteric proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have now quantitatively characterized, in the framework provided by statistical mechanics, the energetics underlying the Ca2+-induced conformational changes that regulate the MthK channel’s open probability.
we have now determined the energetics that govern the Ca2+-induced conformational changes and open probability of the RCK domain from the MthK channel.
we now have a complete and accurate picture of the energetics and kinetics of the conformational changes that occur in a Ca2+-activated K+ channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the energetics for Ca2+-dependent transitions among different conformations of an RCK-domain from the MthK channel, and that the energetics can be used to predict the channel’s open-probability behavior in different Ca2+-concentrations.

we have determined the energetics and kinetics of conformational changes that occur on the angstrom scale in the RCK domain of MthK, and that we have deduced an analytic model that predicts the open probability of the channel from its energetics.
the energetics for Ca2+-dependent gating of the Mthk channel is determined from the conformational states of an RCK domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a minimal set of assumptions, the energetic characteristics of a protein domain can be fully determined from the probabilities of its individual states.
, with the ability to monitor conformational changes, one can determine energetics and, in turn, use the energetics to predict the functional behavior of allosteric proteins.
the energetics governing the conformational transitions in an RCK module are not simply additive but instead are complex and nonintuitive.
